outlooks.summary: SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE TODAY FROM PARTS OF THE LOWER GREAT LAKES AND OHIO VALLEY REGION TO THE CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS...WITH THE GREATEST POTENTIAL ACROSS NORTHERN AND CENTRAL PORTIONS OF ILLINOIS AND INDIANA...AND FAR SOUTHWEST LOWER MICHIGAN.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A MIDLEVEL SPEED MAX WILL CROSS PORTIONS OF THE MIDDLE/UPPER MS VALLEY AND GREAT LAKES REGION ON THE SOUTH SIDE OF A BROAD/AMPLIFYING TROUGH ACROSS THE UPPER/MIDDLE MS VALLEY AND GREAT LAKES REGION. A RELATED SURFACE LOW WILL ADVANCE ACROSS PARTS OF NRN WI AND UPPER MI INTO ADJACENT ONTARIO...REACHING SWRN QUEBEC BY 12Z MONDAY. A COLD FRONT EXTENDING SW OF THE SURFACE LOW TO THE CO ROCKIES FRONT RANGE WILL ADVANCE EAST AND SOUTH TOWARD LOWER MI...INTO THE MIDWEST...LOWER MO VALLEY AND THROUGH THE CENTRAL PLAINS. THE LEADING EDGE OF THE WARM SECTOR WILL ADVANCE NNEWD ACROSS SRN AND ERN PORTIONS OF THE GREAT LAKES REGION...ESTABLISHING A BROAD CORRIDOR OF RICH GULF RETURN MOISTURE AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT. MEANWHILE...A MIDLEVEL TROUGH WILL ELONGATE ENE/WSW OVER PARTS OF THE GREAT BASIN TO CENTRAL ROCKIES...BETWEEN FLANKING RIDGES OVER THE SRN PLAINS AND NWRN STATES.

sections.title: SRN GREAT LAKES/OH AND MID MS VALLEYS
sections.text: AN ONGOING MCS...POSSIBLY PRODUCING STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS...SHOULD BE MOVING THROUGH ERN WI...FAR NRN IL AND WEST-CENTRAL IL PER RECENT HRRR RUNS/00Z NAM/12Z ECMWF. MODERATE-STRONG INSTABILITY IS EXPECTED ACROSS THE WARM SECTOR...GIVEN LOW-LEVEL MOISTENING /SURFACE DEW POINTS IN THE MID-UPPER 60S/ AS FAR EAST AS SRN LOWER MI AND WRN OH AND DIABATIC HEATING. THE LEADING EXTENT OF THE EARLY MORNING MCS SHOULD RE-INTENSIFY IT REACHES SWRN LOWER MI AND NRN IL /INCLUDING THE CHICAGO METRO AREA/ BY EARLY AFTERNOON. EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 30-35 KT ORIENTED GENERALLY PARALLEL TO THE CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY SUGGESTS LINE SEGMENTS/BOWING STRUCTURES AS THE PRIMARY STORM MODE WITH DAMAGING WINDS THE PRIMARY THREAT. HOWEVER...ENHANCED LOW-LEVEL SHEAR ALONG MODESTLY STRONG SWLY LOW-LEVEL WINDS WILL FAVOR A TORNADO THREAT. THE POTENTIAL EXISTS FOR AFTERNOON STORMS TO CONGEAL INTO A WSW/ENE-ELONGATED QUASI-LINEAR MCS THROUGH THE EARLY EVENING HOURS. THIS ACTIVITY SHOULD BE LARGELY ORIENTED PARALLEL TO THE MEAN CLOUD-LAYER FLOW...WHILE GRADUALLY SPREADING ESEWD/SEWD INTO PARTS OF CENTRAL IL...CENTRAL INDIANA...NWRN OH...SERN IL AND PARTS OF WRN OH. DAMAGING WINDS AND MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL W

sections.title: PORTIONS OF NRN/CENTRAL MO WWD TO ERN CO
sections.text: ASCENT SUPPORTING CONVECTION WILL BE PRIMARILY CONFINED TO LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE PROCESSES RELATED TO THE COLD FRONT AND THE TRAILING EXTENT OF THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY ATTENDANT TO THE WI/NRN IL MCS AS IT SETTLES SWD. ISOLATED TO WIDELY SCATTERED TSTMS WILL LIKELY DEVELOP NEAR THESE BOUNDARIES AND WWD TO DIURNALLY ENHANCED OROGRAPHIC CIRCULATIONS OVER THE CO FRONT RANGE AND MOIST/UPSLOPE FLOW TO ITS E. THE PRESENCE OF 25-35 KT OF DEEP SHEAR WILL HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO SUPPORT ORGANIZED/SUSTAINED CONVECTIVE STRUCTURES/POSSIBLE SUPERCELLS. IN THE ABSENCE OF A STRONG EQUATORWARD SURGE OF LOW THETA-E AIR...CONVECTION SHOULD ALSO EVOLVE BEHIND THE COLD FRONT IN PARTS OF E-CNTRL CO INTO NRN KS AND PERHAPS FAR SRN NEB WHERE POST-FRONTAL DIRECTIONAL-FLOW VARIABILITY IN THE LOW-LEVELS WILL BOLSTER DEEP SHEAR /POTENTIAL FOR ORGANIZED STORMS/. A STRENGTHENING SWLY LLJ FROM OK INTO SERN KS AND MO MAY AID IN SUSTAINING TSTMS THROUGH THE EVENING INTO THE EARLY OVERNIGHT PERIOD ACROSS SERN KS TO CENTRAL MO WITH A LINGERING THREAT FOR STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS. ..PETERS/DEAN.. 06/07/2015

outlooks.summary: SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WITH DAMAGING WINDS AND LARGE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE INTO THIS EVENING FROM PARTS OF THE LOWER GREAT LAKES AND OHIO VALLEY REGION TO THE CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS.

sections.title: PRIMARY CHANGES TO THE DAY-1 CONVECTIVE OUTLOOK
sections.text: /1/ PORTIONS OF NRN IL INTO NWRN INDIANA HAVE BEEN UPGRADED TO THE ENHANCED CATEGORY. AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM EARLIER CONVECTION CONTINUES ADVANCING NWD ACROSS NRN IL...IN ADVANCE OF A COLD FRONT APPROACHING THE MS RIVER. THE AIR MASS S OF THE BOUNDARY CONTINUES TO DESTABILIZE. MODIFICATIONS TO THE 18Z ILX RAOB FOR TEMPERATURES IN THE UPPER 80S TO AROUND 90F WITH DEWPOINTS OF 68-71F INDICATE MLCAPE AROUND 2500 J/KG AND LITTLE CINH. CONFIDENCE HAS INCREASED IN A FOCUSED AREA OF CONVECTIVE GENERATION INVOF THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY...ESPECIALLY NEAR THE SYNOPTIC FRONT. GIVEN THE STRONG INSTABILITY IN PLACE...AND H7-H5 LAPSE RATES MEASURED AROUND 6.8 C/KM...INTENSE UPDRAFTS WILL LIKELY ENSUE AS CONVECTION BECOMES SCATTERED TO NUMEROUS IN THE NEXT FEW HOURS. WITH THE ILX AND LOT VWPS INDICATING 1-2-KM-AGL FLOW HOLDING AROUND 30-40 KT AND 35-45 KT OF DEEP SHEAR...CONFIDENCE IS FURTHER BOLSTERED IN STRONG BOWING ELEMENTS CAPABLE OF DMGG WIND GUSTS AS CONVECTION ORGANIZES INTO A QUASI-LINEAR SEGMENT ORIENTED ALONG MEAN CLOUD-LAYER WSWLY FLOW. ONE OR TWO TORNADOES CANNOT BE RULED OUT ACROSS PORTIONS OF NERN IL/NWRN INDIANA WHERE SFC WINDS REMAIN RELATIVELY BACKED ENHANCING LOW-LEVEL STREAMWISE

sections.title: IL/IND/LOWER MI/OH
sections.text: A LARGE LINEAR MCS IS SLOWLY DECAYING ACROSS PARTS OF THE CENTRAL GREAT LAKES REGION. VISIBLE SATELLITE LOOPS SUGGEST THAT CLEARING SKIES BEHIND THE REMNANT MCS WILL HELP TO DESTABILIZE PARTS OF IL/IND/OH AND LOWER MI AS SOUTHWEST SURFACE WINDS TRANSPORT MID 60S DEWPOINTS INTO THE REGION. MOST MODEL SOLUTIONS SUGGEST STORMS BEGIN TO INTENSIFY ALONG AN APPROACHING COLD FRONT OVER NORTHERN IL BY MID AFTERNOON...TRACKING EASTWARD INTO IND/OH/MI DURING THE EVENING. MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES ARE NOT PARTICULARLY STRONG...WHICH MAY LIMIT UPDRAFT STRENGTH. HOWEVER...A WARM/MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER COUPLED WITH 30-40 KNOTS OF WESTERLY FLOW ALOFT WILL PROMOTE GUSTY/DAMAGING WINDS WITH OCCASIONAL BOWING STRUCTURES. STRONGER CELLS MAY ALSO PRODUCE HAIL.

sections.title: MO/ERN KS
sections.text: LATER THIS AFTERNOON AND EARLY EVENING...THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO BUILD WESTWARD ALONG THE COLD FRONT INTO PARTS OF MO AND EVENTUALLY INTO EASTERN KS. EFFECTIVE SHEAR VALUES WILL SUPPORT ORGANIZED MULTICELL STORMS. A DEEP-MIXED BOUNDARY LAYER AHEAD OF THE FRONT ALONG WITH RELATIVELY STEEP MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES SUGGEST THE RISK OF DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL IN THE STRONGER STORMS THROUGH THE EVENING.

sections.title: ERN CO/WRN KS
sections.text: MORNING SURFACE ANALYSIS SHOWS A COLD FRONT SAGGING SOUTHWARD ACROSS NORTHWEST KS...EXTENDING BACK TO THE FOOTHILLS OF CO. THIS FRONT WILL CONTINUE TO MOVE SOUTHWARD TODAY...WITH NORTHWEST SURFACE WINDS THROUGHOUT THE AFTERNOON ACROSS PARTS OF WY/NEB/CO/WRN KS. STRONG HEATING AND STEEP LOW/MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL LIKELY RESULT IN ISOLATED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT IN THE NW FLOW REGIME...ALONG WITH ISOLATED HIGH-BASED STORMS IN THE PRE-FRONTAL ENVIRONMENT. ACTIVITY WILL TRACK INTO EASTERN CO/WESTERN KS BY EARLY EVENING...WHERE SUFFICIENT DEEP LAYER SHEAR MAY RESULT IN A SUPERCELL OR TWO CAPABLE OF HAIL AND GUSTY WINDS.

outlooks.summary: SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WITH DAMAGING WINDS AND LARGE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE THROUGH THIS EVENING TO THE EARLY OVERNIGHT HOURS FROM PARTS OF THE OHIO VALLEY THROUGH THE LOWER MISSOURI VALLEY TO EASTERN KANSAS. OTHER ISOLATED STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE ACROSS THE CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A MID- TO UPPER-LEVEL TROUGH CURRENTLY EXTENDING FROM ONTARIO THROUGH THE UPPER MIDWEST TO NEB WILL CONTINUE TO AMPLIFY ESEWD TONIGHT INTO THE GREAT LAKES TO LOWER MO/MID MS VALLEYS REGION. RELATED SURFACE LOW WILL MOVE ACROSS CENTRAL ONTARIO TOWARD SWRN QUEBEC THROUGH 12Z MONDAY...WHILE THE ATTENDANT COLD FRONT ADVANCES EAST AND SOUTH INTO LOWER MI...NRN IL...NRN AND CENTRAL MO AND THROUGH KS. PRE-FRONTAL BOUNDARIES OVER NERN KS...NWRN OK TO ERN KS AND NRN MO...AND A COUPLE OF CONVECTIVE BOUNDARIES ATTENDANT TO ONGOING QUASI-LINEAR MCS/S IN PARTS OF NRN/CENTRAL IND TO ERN IL...AND THE SECOND FROM CENTRAL IL TO NERN MO...WILL REMAIN THE PRIMARY FOCI FOR ADDITIONAL SEVERE STORMS THROUGH THIS EVENING INTO THE EARLY OVERNIGHT HOURS. MEANWHILE...A MIDLEVEL IMPULSE THAT MOVED EWD FROM SERN CO INTO SWRN KS TO THE OK/NRN TX PANHANDLES AND A SEPARATE APPARENT MIDLEVEL IMPULSE/SUB-TROPICAL JETLET CURRENTLY PHASING WITH THE FORMER IMPULSE SHOULD PROGRESS EWD THIS FORECAST PERIOD ACROSS SRN KS/NRN OK.

sections.title: OH/MID MS VALLEYS
sections.text: AFTERNOON STORMS HAVE CONTINUED TO CONGEAL INTO TWO ENE/WSW-ELONGATED QUASI-LINEAR MCS/S...WITH THE FIRST CURRENTLY EXTENDING FROM FAR NWRN OH THROUGH NRN INDIANA TO EAST-CENTRAL IL...WHILE THE LEADING EXTENT OF THE SECOND MCS NEARLY OVERLAPPED THE TRAILING PORTION OF THE FIRST MCS AND EXTENDED WWD THROUGH NRN MO. THIS ACTIVITY IS LARGELY ORIENTED PARALLEL TO THE MEAN CLOUD-LAYER FLOW...AND WILL CONTINUE TO ADVANCE ESEWD/SEWD INTO THE REST OF NERN TO EAST-CENTRAL MO...CENTRAL IL...CENTRAL INDIANA AND WRN OH. THE SLIGHT RISK AREA HAS BEEN EXPANDED EWD SOME TO INCLUDE MORE OF WRN OH. DAMAGING WINDS AND MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL WILL REMAIN THE MAIN THREATS...WITH A TORNADO THREAT POSSIBLE...GIVEN RESIDUAL MODERATE-STRONG INSTABILITY. THE ENHANCED SEVERE RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS HAS BEEN RE-ORIENTED ALONG AND DOWNSTREAM OF THE TWO MCS/S FOR THE SHORT TERM.

sections.title: ERN KS/WRN-CENTRAL MO
sections.text: REMNANTS OF THE NWD RETURN OF RICH GULF MOISTURE PERSIST ACROSS ERN KS AND WRN-CENTRAL MO WITH SURFACE DEW POINTS GENERALLY IN THE UPPER 60S TO AROUND 70 F. THIS MOISTURE COMBINED WITH THE EWD EXTENT OF STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES AND STRONG DIABATIC HEATING TODAY HAS RESULTED IN A RESERVOIR OF MODERATE-STRONG INSTABILITY /MLCAPE UP TO 2000-2500 J PER KG/ IN THE WARM SECTOR NEAR AND SOUTH OF THE AFOREMENTIONED COLD FRONT AND PRE-FRONTAL BOUNDARIES. GRADUAL HEIGHT FALLS WITH THE MAIN MID/UPPER-LEVEL TROUGH AMPLIFYING INTO THIS REGION...FORCING FOR ASCENT ATTENDANT TO THE SUB-TROPICAL IMPULSE...AND ASCENT ALONG SWD MOVING BOUNDARIES SHOULD AID IN ADDITIONAL STORMS DEVELOPING ACROSS THE REST OF ERN KS AND NRN INTO CENTRAL MO THROUGH THE EARLY OVERNIGHT PERIOD. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE THE PRIMARY THREATS...THOUGH AN INCREASE IN LOW-LEVEL SHEAR ALONG A STRENGTHENING SWLY LLJ FROM SERN KS TO CENTRAL MO SUGGESTS A TORNADO THREAT CANNOT BE RULED OUT. ..PETERS.. 06/08/2015

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A MARGINAL THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL AND GUSTY WINDS WILL EXIST THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. A WW IS UNLIKELY AT THIS TIME.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWS MOSTLY CLOUD-FREE CONDITIONS ACROSS MUCH OF ERN NM...WHICH WILL ALLOW DIURNAL HEATING TO CONTINUE TO WARM THE LOW-LEVELS OF THE ATMOSPHERE. AS SFC TEMPERATURES INCREASE TO THE 80S AND PERHAPS LOWER 90S IN THE PRESENCE OF DEWPOINTS IN THE MID 50S TO LOWER 60S...MLCAPE OF 1000-1500 J/KG SHOULD BE COMMON ACROSS THE MCD REGION...WITH UP TO 2000 J/KG POSSIBLE. A BELT OF ENHANCED MID TO UPPER LEVEL FLOW ASSOCIATED WITH AN UPPER LOW OVER UT SHOULD PROVIDE ONLY A GLANCING INFLUENCE OVER ERN NM AND THE TX/OK PANHANDLES...WITH 25-35 KT OF WSWLY WINDS AT 500 MB COMMON OVER THIS AREA PER RAP ANALYSIS. CONVECTION HAS RECENTLY INITIATED OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF CNTRL NM...AND VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SUGGESTS THIS ACTIVITY WILL MOVE ENE INTO ERN NM AND THE WRN PORTIONS OF THE TX/OK PANHANDLES WITH TIME. WHILE THE LOW-LEVEL WIND FIELD IS NOT FORECAST TO BE PARTICULARLY STRONG...A VEERING/STRENGTHENING WIND PROFILE WITH HEIGHT...EVIDENCED BY 30-35 KT OF EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR...SHOULD ALLOW SOME OF THESE THUNDERSTORMS TO ORGANIZE/ROTATE. ANY OF THESE STRONGER THUNDERSTORMS WILL POSE A THREAT OF LARGE HAIL AND PERHAPS GUSTY WINDS. HOWEVER...DUE TO THE MARGINAL WIND FIELD/BULK SHEAR AND ISOLATED EXPECTED SEVERE THREAT...A WW WILL PROBABLY NOT BE NEEDED.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A SEVERE THREAT IS EXPECTED TO DEVELOP FROM NRN MO AND SERN IA EWD ACROSS NCNTRL IL OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. LARGE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE WILL BE POSSIBLE AS CELLS INITIATE AND INCREASE IN COVERAGE. WW ISSUANCE LIKELY BE NEEDED FOR PARTS OF THIS AREA THIS AFTERNOON.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THE LATEST SFC ANALYSIS SHOWS A COLD FRONT EXTENDING FROM CNTRL WI SWWD INTO SRN IA...FAR SE NEB AND NRN KS. AHEAD OF THE BOUNDARY...SFC DEWPOINTS ARE GENERALLY IN THE UPPER 60S AND LOWER 70S F WITH TEMPS FROM THE MID 80S TO THE LOWER 90S F. THIS IS CONTRIBUTING TO A POCKET OF MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY WITH MLCAPE ESTIMATED TO BE IN THE 2000 TO 3000 J/KG RANGE ACROSS MUCH OF THE MCD AREA. IN ADDITION...WATER VAPOR IMAGERY SHOWS A SUBTLE SHORTWAVE TROUGH MOVING INTO NRN MO WHICH WILL AID CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON. THE HRRR AND OTHER SHORT-TERM MODEL FORECASTS APPEAR TO DEVELOP SFC-BASED STORMS FROM NEAR THE IA-MO STATELINE EWD INTO NCNTRL IL OVER THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS WHERE LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE IS ENHANCED. IN ADDITION...WSR-88D VWPS ACROSS CNTRL AND NRN IL SHOW SOME DIRECTIONAL SHEAR IN THE LOW-LEVELS WITH 40 TO 45 KT OF FLOW AT MID-LEVELS...RESULTING IN 40 TO 50 KT OF 0-6 KM SHEAR. THIS SHOULD SUPPORT A SEVERE THREAT AS CELLS INITIATE AND EXPAND IN COVERAGE THIS AFTERNOON. HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH CELLS THAT ROTATE. WIND DAMAGE MAY ALSO OCCUR WITH THE BETTER ORGANIZED LINE SEGMENTS. THE WIND DAMAGE THREAT COULD INCREASE ESPECIALLY IF A COLD POOL CAN ORGANIZE ACROSS THE REGION LATER THIS AFTERNOON INTO EARLY EVENING.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE SEVERE WEATHER THREAT IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE THE MAIN THREATS. WW ISSUANCE IS POSSIBLE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: TWO AREAS OF CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT SEEM PROBABLE ACROSS THE MCD AREA THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING. THE FIRST AREA WILL BE ALONG OR JUST N OF A SLOWLY SWD MOVING COLD FRONT/WIND SHIFT CURRENTLY LOCATED ACROSS SERN CO INTO SWRN KS. THUNDERSTORMS HAVE INCREASED IN COVERAGE OVER THE PAST HOUR IN SERN CO AS BROAD LIFT ASSOCIATED WITH AN APPROACHING WIND MAXIMUM AT THE UPPER LEVELS INTERACTS WITH THE COLD FRONT. SFC TEMPERATURES IN SERN CO/SWRN KS HAVE GENERALLY WARMED INTO THE LOW TO MID 80S...WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE 50S. A SECOND AREA OF CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT SHOULD EVENTUALLY OCCUR OVER NERN CO/SWRN NEB...WHERE VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY DEPICTS AN AREA OF AGITATED CU POSSIBLY ASSOCIATED WITH OUTFLOW FROM PRIOR CONVECTION...IN ADDITION TO DEVELOPMENT OCCURRING ALONG THE FRONT RANGE IN CO. IN THIS POST-FRONTAL REGIME...SFC TEMPERATURES ARE IN THE MID TO UPPER 70S AND DEWPOINTS RANGE FROM THE MID 40S TO MID 50S. WEAK LOW-LEVEL COLD AIR ADVECTION SHOULD TEMPER DIURNAL HEATING SOMEWHAT ACROSS THIS AREA THROUGH THE AFTERNOON...BUT MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AROUND 7.0-8.0 DEG C/KM SHOULD ENCOURAGE MLCAPE OF 500-1000 J/KG OVER THIS REGION. ENHANCED MID-LEVEL FLOW SHOULD SUPPORT EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR VALUES OF 40-50 KT ACROSS THE MCD AREA. THIS SHOULD ENABLE ANY THUNDERSTORMS THAT FORM TO ACQUIRE SUPERCELL CHARACTERISTICS...WITH AN ASSOCIATED THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS. IN BETWEEN THE TWO AREAS DESCRIBED ABOVE...NAMELY E-CNTRL CO INTO W-CNTRL KS...THERE SEEMS TO BE A RELATIVE MINIMUM IN CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT IN MOST RECENT CAM GUIDANCE. THIS SUGGESTS THAT PERHAPS ONLY A SUBSET OF THE OVERALL MCD AREA MAY NEED A WW OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A SEVERE THREAT WILL DEVELOP ACROSS PARTS OF CNTRL AND NRN IND OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE MAY OCCUR AS CELLS MOVE SEWD INTO CNTRL IND LATE THIS AFTERNOON. A WW WILL BE ISSUED SHORTLY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THE LATEST SFC ANALYSIS SHOWS SSWLY FLOW ACROSS MUCH OF THE OH VALLEY AND SRN GREAT LAKES REGION WITH A MOIST AIRMASS IN PLACE IN CNTRL IL AND WRN IND. SFC DEWPOINTS ARE IN THE MID 60S TO LOWER 70S F ALONG THIS CORRIDOR WHERE MODERATE INSTABILITY IS ANALYZED. IN ADDITION...THE WSR-88D VWP AT INDIANAPOLIS SHOWS VEERED LOW-LEVEL WINDS WITH 40 KT OF WLY FLOW AT 4 KM. THIS IS CREATING MODERATE DEEP-LAYER SHEAR WHICH WILL SUPPORT SEVERE THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT LATE THIS AFTERNOON. ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE WILL BE THE PRIMARY THREATS WITH THE ACTIVITY.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AT LEAST ISOLATED STORM INITIATION IS POSSIBLE IN THE NEXT 1-2 HRS...WITH A RISK OF LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND. WATCH ISSUANCE IS POSSIBLE IF CONVECTIVE TRENDS FAVOR THE POTENTIAL FOR MULTIPLE ORGANIZED SEVERE CELLS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: DESPITE STRONG DIURNAL HEATING...CONVECTION HAS BEEN SLOW TO DEVELOP ACROSS CNTRL INTO NERN KS THUS FAR...LIKELY DUE TO WEAK FRONTAL CONVERGENCE AND MINIMAL LARGE-SCALE ASCENT ACROSS THE AREA. HOWEVER...LATEST 1-MINUTE SUPER-RAPID SCAN VIS IMAGERY DEPICTS A COUPLE OF CORRIDORS OF DEEPENING CU...ONE ALONG A PREFRONTAL WIND SHIFT FROM NORTH OF ICT TO NEAR MCI...AND THE OTHER ALONG THE MAIN BAROCLINIC ZONE FROM NEAR RSL TO CNK TO FNB...WITH CG LTG RECENTLY NOTED NORTH OF RSL FROM A DEVELOPING UPDRAFT. WITH MODERATE-TO-STRONG INSTABILITY AND SUFFICIENT EFFECTIVE SHEAR IN PLACE ACROSS THE REGION...ORGANIZED STORM STRUCTURES ARE POSSIBLE IF DEEP CONVECTION CAN INITIATE...WITH A FEW SUPERCELLS AND/OR BOWING SEGMENTS POSSIBLE. LARGE HAIL WOULD BE POSSIBLE WITH ANY SUPERCELL...WHILE A DAMAGING WIND RISK WILL EXIST WITH ANY STORM MODE GIVEN THE STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES IN PLACE AHEAD OF THE FRONT. PRIMARY UNCERTAINTY REGARDING WW ISSUANCE IS THE COVERAGE OF THE SEVERE THREAT...BUT A WATCH MAY BE REQUIRED IF THE THREAT OF MULTIPLE ORGANIZED SEVERE STORMS APPEARS IMMINENT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: NUMEROUS SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WILL CONTINUE ACROSS THE WATCH AREAS IN THE FORM OF LINES/BOWING SEGMENTS AND SEMI-DISCRETE STORMS. THE MORE PRONOUNCED WIND DAMAGE THREAT IN THE SHORT TERM WILL BE WITH PRONOUNCED BOWING SEGMENT OVER NORTHWEST INDIANA. A LOCAL WATCH EXTENSION MAY BE NEEDED WITH TIME TO THE EAST OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH 270...AND A NEW WATCH MAY BE NEEDED SOUTHEAST OF THIS WATCH LATER THIS EVENING.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: NUMEROUS SVR TSTMS WERE IN PROGRESS AT 2225Z FROM NWRN IND SWWD ACROSS W-CENTRAL IL...WITH A HISTORY OF DAMAGING WINDS AND LARGE HAIL. THE DOMINANT CONVECTIVE MODE OVER MUCH OF THE AREA RECENTLY HAS BEEN LINEAR...WITH A PRONOUNCED BOWING SEGMENT OVER FAR NWRN IND SHOWING A WELL-DEVELOPED COMMA HEAD AND REAR INFLOW JET. DAMAGING WINDS ARE LIKELY...WITH A FEW SIGNIFICANT SVR WIND REPORTS POSSIBLE AS THIS SEGMENT OF THE LINE CONTINUES TO MOVE EWD WITHIN A FAVORABLY SHEARED/MODERATELY BUOYANT ENVIRONMENT. WITH TIME...A LOCAL EXTENSION OF WW 270 MAY BE NEEDED TO THE E OF CURRENT WATCH AREA. IN ADDITION...A NEW WATCH MAY BE REQUIRED TO THE SOUTHEAST OF THIS WATCH LATER THIS EVENING. SVR TSTMS EXTENDING ACROSS CENTRAL/W-CENTRAL IL WITHIN WW 267 REMAIN A MIX OF LINEAR AND SEMI-DISCRETE CELLS. MESOANALYSIS AND RECENT VWP DATA REFLECT 40-45 KTS OF EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR WITH MODERATE/STRONG SURFACE-BASED INSTABILITY. GIVEN BROAD/WEAK HEIGHT FALLS ASSOCIATED WITH AN UPSTREAM SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVERSPREADING THE AREA...THE ENVIRONMENT WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT A SVR THREAT INTO THE EVENING HOURS. ..BUNTING.. 06/07/2015 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE THREAT FOR ISOLATED SEVERE HAIL/WIND CONTINUES IN AND NEAR WW 268. AN ISOLATED DAMAGING-WIND THREAT WILL EXPAND OUT OF THE WATCH INTO NWRN OK...BUT DOWNSTREAM WW ISSUANCE IS NOT ANTICIPATED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AT 2315Z...SCATTERED STRONG/POTENTIALLY SEVERE STORMS ARE ONGOING ACROSS MAINLY THE SERN HALF OF WW 268...WITH A MEASURED GUST TO 54 KTS OBSERVED AT 2235Z IN BEAVER COUNTY OK. THE STORM CLUSTER THAT PRODUCED THAT SEVERE WIND GUST IS NOW MOVING OUT OF THE WATCH INTO NWRN OK. A LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND RISK WILL PERSIST WITH THIS CLUSTER FOR NEXT 1-2 HRS GIVEN THE VERY WARM AND WELL-MIXED BOUNDARY LAYER...BUT RELATIVELY WEAK EFFECTIVE SHEAR AND LOW-LEVEL FLOW /AS NOTED ON 21Z LMN SOUNDING/ SHOULD LIMIT THE LONGEVITY OF THIS SYSTEM...AND DOWNSTREAM WW ISSUANCE IS NOT ANTICIPATED. ELSEWHERE ACROSS WW 268...CONVECTION HAS DEVELOPED INTO SEVERAL SMALL BOWING SEGMENTS ACROSS NERN NM INTO THE TX/OK PANHANDLES...WITH AN ASSOCIATED RISK OF DAMAGING WINDS. HOWEVER...THE TENDENCY FOR OUTFLOW TO SURGE AHEAD OF THE STRONGEST CONVECTIVE ELEMENTS MAY TEMPER THE WIND THREAT SOMEWHAT. MEANWHILE...REDEVELOPMENT IS POSSIBLE ACROSS THE NWRN PART OF WW 268 IN NERN NM/SERN CO...AND ONGOING STORMS ACROSS E-CNTRL CO MAY MOVE SEWD INTO THE WATCH AFTER 00Z...WITH AN ISOLATED WIND/HAIL RISK. ..DEAN.. 06/07/2015 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE SEVERE WEATHER THREAT WILL CONTINUE ACROSS REMAINING VALID PORTIONS OF THE WATCH AREA.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SVR TSTMS CONTINUE IN ADVANCE OF A WEAK COLD FRONT...MAINLY ACROSS THE ERN TWO-THIRDS OF THE WW AREA. THE TSTMS ARE ALONG THE SRN FRINGE OF STRONGER DEEP-LAYER SHEAR ORIENTED GENERALLY PARALLEL TO THE TSTMS. WITH MODERATE/STRONG SFC-BASED INSTABILITY IN PLACE...THIS HAS LED TO A MIX OF LINEAR AND SEMI-DISCRETE STORM MODES PRODUCING BOTH LARGE HAIL AND OCNL SVR GUSTS. STRONGER BOWING SEGMENTS MAY DEVELOP THROUGH 02Z WITH CORRIDORS OF MORE CONCENTRATED WIND DAMAGE MAINLY ACROSS NERN MO/W-CENTRAL IL. MORE ISOLD TSTM DEVELOPMENT CONTINUES ACROSS FAR WRN PORTIONS OF WW AREA TO THE E OF KSTJ...WHERE KEAX RADAR AND GOES 1-MIN VIS IMAGERY SHOWS A COUPLE SLOWLY INTENSIFYING CELLS. AS WEAK HEIGHT FALLS GLANCE THE AREA THIS EVENING...THESE STORMS MAY ALSO INTENSIFY TO SVR LEVELS. THIS SCENARIO IS SUPPORTED BY RECENT HIGH-RES GUIDANCE INCLUDING THE NCEP-HRRR AND NSSL WRF. ..BUNTING.. 06/07/2015 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE THREAT OF DAMAGING WINDS EXISTS ACROSS MAINLY THE SOUTHERN HALF OF THE WATCH AREA.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A LINE OF SVR TSTMS FROM HOWARD COUNTY SOUTHWEST INTO MONTGOMERY COUNTY INDIANA CONTINUES TO MOVE ESE AT AROUND 35 KTS. WITH A WELL-DEVELOPED COLD POOL AND FAVORABLY SHEARED ENVIRONMENT...THIS LINE IS LIKELY TO CONTINUE TO PRODUCE DAMAGING WINDS AS IT MOVES ACROSS SRN PORTIONS OF THE WW AREA. IN ADDITION...UPSTREAM SVR TSTMS ABOUT TO EXIT WW 267 WILL ALSO MOVE INTO SWRN PORTIONS OF WW 271 IN THE 01-02Z TIME FRAME. ALTHOUGH THE GREATEST SVR THREAT IS EXPECTED TO SHIFT SEWD ACROSS WW 271 DURING THE SHORT TERM...CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED FARTHER E FOR THE POSSIBILITY OF A NEW WW INTO NWRN OH. ..BUNTING.. 06/08/2015 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND CONTINUES ACROSS WW 272.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AT 0230Z...A LONG-LIVED SUPERCELL WITH A HISTORY OF PRODUCING LARGE HAIL WAS APPROACHING EMPORIA KS...WHILE ADDITIONAL STORMS WERE DEVELOPING ON THE WRN FLANK OF THIS STORM. THIS ACTIVITY MAY PERSIST FOR ANOTHER 1-2 HRS WITH A CONTINUED RISK OF LARGE HAIL AND LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND...THOUGH INCREASING CINH WILL RESULT IN AN INCREASINGLY HOSTILE ENVIRONMENT FOR DISCRETE SUPERCELLS. SOME WEAKENING HAS RECENTLY BEEN NOTED WITH THIS ACTIVITY. FURTHER EAST...THE TAIL END OF AN ELONGATED QLCS WAS MOVING ACROSS THE ERN PORTION OF THE WATCH. THIS ACTIVITY IS BEING AIDED BY A SWLY 30-40 KT LOW-LEVEL JET /AS NOTED ON KEAX VWP/. SOME BACKBUILDING TO THE WEST INTO FAR ERN KS IS POSSIBLE WITH TIME AS THE LLJ-DRIVEN WAA CONTINUES ALONG THE SWD-MOVING COMPOSITE OUTFLOW/FRONTAL BOUNDARY. ISOLATED INSTANCES OF LARGE HAIL/DAMAGING WIND WILL BE POSSIBLE...THOUGH THE INCREASINGLY ANAFRONTAL NATURE OF THE CONVECTION WILL BEGIN TO TEMPER THE SEVERE THREAT OVERALL. A HEAVY RAIN THREAT WILL ALSO EXIST WITH THIS ACTIVITY...SEE MPD 183 FROM WPC FOR MORE DETAILS. ..DEAN.. 06/08/2015 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE SEVERE WEATHER THREAT CONTINUES ACROSS REMAINING VALID PORTIONS OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH 271 AND 273.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STRONG/SVR TSTMS CONTINUE ACROSS MAINLY SRN PORTIONS OF WW 271 AND 273 AT 0245Z...WITH AN EMBEDDED BOWING SEGMENT PRODUCING AN ENHANCED WIND DAMAGE THREAT VCTY VERMILLION/DOUGLAS/EDGAR COUNTIES IN ILLINOIS. IN ADDITION TO DAMAGING WINDS...EMBEDDED QLCS CIRCULATIONS WILL ALSO CONTINUE TO POSE A SHORT-LIVED TORNADO THREAT. THE ONSET OF NOCTURNAL COOLING...AND CORRESPONDING INCREASE IN CINH...IS EVIDENT ON LATEST MESOANALYSIS ACROSS MUCH OF THE WATCH AREAS...SUGGESTING THAT WITH TIME STRONGER GUSTS MAY HAVE AN INCREASINGLY DIFFICULT TIME MAKING IT TO THE SFC. THE EXCEPTION IS AHEAD OF THE LINE OVER CENTRAL IL EWD INTO W-CENTRAL INDIANA...WHERE NEGLIGIBLE CINH IS INDICATED AND WHERE THE GREATEST SHORT-TERM SVR THREAT EXISTS. WITH THE RECENT SWD SURGE OF TSTMS IN THESE AREAS ASSOCIATED WITH BOWING SEGMENT JUST E OF CHAMPAIGN IL...LOCAL WW EXTENSION SOUTH OF WW AREAS MAY BE NEEDED...APPROXIMATELY FROM EFFINGHAM CO IL EWD TO OWEN CO INDIANA. ..BUNTING.. 06/08/2015 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND A TORNADO CONTINUES ACROSS REMAINING VALID PORTIONS OF THE WATCH AREA. A LOCAL EXTENSION IN AREA AND TIME MAY BE NEEDED PRIOR TO THE SCHEDULED 05Z EXPIRATION.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A PRONOUNCED BOWING COMPLEX OF SVR TSTMS CONTINUES MOVING EWD AT 35-40 KTS ACROSS W-CENTRAL INDIANA/E-CENTRAL IL AT 04Z...EXTENDING GENERALLY FROM MONTGOMERY CO INDIANA TO CLARK COUNTY IL. RECENT RADAR REFLECTIVITY SUGGESTS A NRN BOOKEND VORTEX MAY BE DEVELOPING...AND A REAR INFLOW JET MAY BE BECOMING ESTABLISHED. IF THESE TRENDS CONTINUE...THIS BOWING COMPLEX MAY CONTINUE TO PRODUCE CORRIDORS OF ENHANCED WIND DAMAGE AND SHORT-LIVED QLCS TORNADOES BEYOND THE SCHEDULED EXPIRATION TIME OF WW 271 AT 05Z. IN ADDITION...THE THREAT MAY SHIFT S OF THE CURRENT SRN WATCH AREA...IN CLOSER PROXIMITY TO HIGHER THETA-E AIR AND A 40-45 KT LOW LEVEL JET. AS A RESULT A LOCAL AREAL/TEMPORAL EXTENSION OF THE WW MAY BE NEEDED ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE WFO IND CWA. BEYOND 06-07Z...THE THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS SHOULD DIMINISH...HOWEVER CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED. ..BUNTING.. 06/08/2015 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND LARGE HAIL EXISTS WITHIN THE REMAINING VALID PORTIONS OF THE WATCH AREA.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: COMPOSITE RADAR IMAGERY AT 0430Z SHOWS A BROKEN LINE OF TSTMS EXTENDING FROM BOONE CO MO WWD ACROSS THE KANSAS CITY AREA AND FAR ERN KS. RADAR ALSO INDICATES THAT A GUST FRONT HAS SURGED SWD IN ADVANCE OF THE TSTMS...RESULTING IN MOSTLY NON-SVR STORMS ROOTED ABOVE THE INCREASINGLY STABLE BOUNDARY LAYER. WITH 35-40 KTS OF MID-LEVEL FLOW AND MUCAPE OF 1000 -1500 J/KG IN THE BACKGROUND ENVIRONMENT...AT LEAST SOME SVR THREAT REMAINS ACROSS THE REMAINING PORTIONS OF THE WW AREA WITH THE STRONGEST STORMS. OVERALL...HOWEVER...THE THREAT IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN ISOLATED. ..BUNTING.. 06/08/2015 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...
